name: What is the difference between a temperature relief valve and a pressure relief valve?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a temperature relief valve and a pressure relief valve?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often referred to interchangeably, a water heater's pressure relief valve (PRV) is primarily designed to release water if pressure becomes too high, while a temperature relief valve (TRV) opens if the water temperature exceeds a safe limit. Most modern water heaters, however, use a single combination valve called a Temperature and Pressure Relief Valve (TPRV) that reacts to both conditions, offering comprehensive safety. When CG Plumbing Solutions replaces your valve, we install a new TPRV that addresses both potential hazards, ensuring your water heater operates safely according to current plumbing codes.
acceptedAnswer.description: A PRV reacts to high pressure, a TRV to high temperature; most modern units use a combined TPRV for both functions.
